```{r}
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(arrow)
library(lubridate)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
```


I want to illustrate the mechanism of cross border saturation.
On 2018-01-02, French and Spanish prices are equal and comove perfectly,
until the Cross border capacity is saturated (to about 3000),
then there are separate prices.



```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/DBT3KD/Desktop/Etude_macro_elec/prix_electricite_gitlab/day_ahead/outputs/cross_border")
price_merge_CBF <- read_parquet( "price_merge_CBF.parquet")

price_merge_CBF <-price_merge_CBF %>% 
  mutate(SCH_EX_DA_FR_ES = as.numeric(SCH_EX_DA_FR_ES),
         SCH_EX_DA_ES_FR = as.numeric(SCH_EX_DA_ES_FR),
         SCH_EX_TOT_FR_ES = as.numeric(SCH_EX_TOT_FR_ES),
         SCH_EX_TOT_ES_FR = as.numeric(SCH_EX_TOT_ES_FR),
        SCH_EX_Spread_FR_ES = SCH_EX_TOT_FR_ES - SCH_EX_DA_FR_ES ,
         SCH_EX_Spread_ES_FR = SCH_EX_TOT_ES_FR - SCH_EX_DA_ES_FR,
         price_diff_fr_esp = price_fr - price_esp,
         #contrary to CBF I allow for negative CBF
         # with the convention that ESP to FR is >0
         CBF_DA = SCH_EX_DA_ES_FR - SCH_EX_DA_FR_ES
         )

colnames_with_capacity <- colnames(price_merge_CBF)[grepl("Capacity", colnames(price_merge_CBF))]
#get monthly avg of unavailabilities
capacity_fields <- 
  c(colnames_with_capacity,
    "day_ahead_forecast_esp",  "unpredicted_renewables_esp", "intraday_update_renewables_esp",
  "day_ahead_forecast_fr",  "unpredicted_renewables_fr", "intraday_update_renewables_fr")

price_merge_CBF[colnames_with_capacity] <- lapply(price_merge_CBF[colnames_with_capacity], function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x))

price_merge_CBF$weekday <- weekdays(price_merge_CBF$delivery_date)


```



```{r}
plot_example <- price_merge_CBF %>% 
  filter(delivery_date == "2019-01-02" | delivery_date =="2019-01-03")

ggplot(data = plot_example, aes(x = datetime))+
  geom_line(aes(y = price_fr*20, color = "FR"))+
  geom_line(aes(y = price_esp*20, color = "ES"))+
  geom_line(aes(y = NTC_ESP_FR, color = "ES -> FR"), linetype ="dashed")+
  geom_line(aes(y = NTC_FR_ESP, color = "FR -> ES"), linetype ="dashed")+
  geom_line(aes(y = SCH_EX_DA_ES_FR, color = "ES -> FR"))+
  geom_line(aes(y = SCH_EX_DA_FR_ES, color = "FR -> ES"))+
    # Mise en place de l'échelle secondaire pour les prix
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "NTC & Exchanges",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 20, name = "Price (€/MWh)") # Ajuste l'échelle inverse
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal()

  
```

Faire apparaître le seuil de saturation




```{r}

price_merge_CBF <- price_merge_CBF %>% 
       mutate(
         Taux_Sat_ES_FR = SCH_EX_DA_ES_FR/NTC_ESP_FR,
         Taux_Sat_FR_ES = SCH_EX_DA_FR_ES/NTC_FR_ESP) %>% 
  filter(Taux_Sat_FR_ES<1.1 & Taux_Sat_ES_FR<1.1) %>%
  mutate(
         saturation_bin_ES_FR = ntile(Taux_Sat_ES_FR, 100),
         saturation_bin_FR_ES = ntile(Taux_Sat_FR_ES, 100)
       )

plot_data_ES_FR <- price_merge_CBF %>%
  group_by(saturation_bin_ES_FR) %>%
  summarize(
    taux_saturation_moyen = mean(SCH_EX_DA_ES_FR/NTC_ESP_FR, na.rm = TRUE),
    price_diff_moyen = mean(price_diff_fr_esp, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) 

ggplot(data =plot_data_ES_FR ,aes(x = taux_saturation_moyen, y = price_diff_moyen)) +
geom_point() +
labs(x = "Taux de saturation", y = TeX('$\\Delta p$')) +
theme_minimal()
```
